## [2026-10-10](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-10.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12086>)

EvoAlloc learns when a program-search agent should spend resources evaluating a candidate, revising its allocation rules as results accumulate. Occasionally testing rejected candidates reveals missed opportunities, helping the search reach useful solutions with fewer evaluations.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-09T10:11:06Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Program Evolution, Evaluation Allocation, Agent Self-Improvement

**Public availability:** 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12086>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery from the October 9 NEW batch. Five-seed matched-target comparisons in Table 5 reduce ADAS-AIME evaluation calls from 69 to 28 and LLM tokens from 89.8M to 35.3M. V1: 2026-10-08T14:57:35Z.

**Limitations:** Only two benchmarks; search and assessment share the same 30 AIME problems. Initial 50 baseline cases are excluded from cost. At the full evaluation budget, total tokens increase. Code is promised upon acceptance; results were not reproduced.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629>)

ReAct alternates reasoning, environment actions, and observations so an agent can revise its plan using external evidence. It remains a useful foundation for tool-using agent loops because task execution and information gathering become part of the reasoning process.

**Published:** 2022-10-06 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Planning, Tool Use, Grounding

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629>) · [Project](<https://react-lm.github.io/>) · [Code](<https://github.com/ysymyth/ReAct>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The ICLR camera-ready paper compares reasoning-only, acting-only and interleaved policies on question answering, fact verification and interactive tasks; its ablations and failure analysis make the control pattern inspectable. The arXiv history records v1 on October 6, 2022 and v3 on March 10, 2023.

**Limitations:** This is a foundational method, not a claim of current benchmark leadership. Retrieval failures and repetitive loops remain possible; ReAct alone trails chain-of-thought on the reported HotpotQA setting.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147>)

This work separates task execution from a controller that assesses accumulated work, proposes next steps, evaluates their value, and dispatches workers using persistent artifact memory. It offers a way to spend larger inference budgets more effectively on long tasks by choosing which partial results to reuse, repair, or abandon.

**Published:** 2026-09-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Planning, Test-Time Scaling, Memory, Long-Horizon

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3, 5 and 6 provide the controller design and matched-worker comparisons across four benchmarks and three models; reported ProgramBench performance is 71.5% with GPT-5.5 versus 58.0% for Codex. Submission history verifies September 29, 2026 at 17:57:25 UTC.

**Limitations:** A new preprint with no independent reproduction here. Equal model-call allowances do not equal token, latency or FLOP budgets; control overhead hurts at small budgets, and the design underperforms direct control on the LongCoT-mini chess subset.
